messages:
anna_dev: Heads-up — our apples-to-apples replay vs synthetic load numbers are diverging badly, replay p50 ~18ms, synthetic/clients show ~40ms. Did a quick check and logs look clean.

mike_infra: Are you replaying from the exact same packet sizes/concurrency? small client differences can push different kernel selection paths.

anna_dev: Using replay-harness v0.9 (same model weights/seq). Concurrency/arrival distribution are identical AFAICT. Batching histogram shows different effective batch sizes on the server.

jiwon_ml: Kernel selection toggles at certain seq+batch thresholds. If client bursts group requests differently we fall into slower matmul kernels. Could explain p50 shift.

sarah_sre: Also check TCP keepalive / connection pooling on the client. If each req opens a new TLS session it explodes tail latency.

mike_infra: +1. I saw replay harness reuses long-lived HTTP/2 streams, but our synthetic client spawns N connections and relies on OS to reuse ports. That causes more TLS handshakes and slow starts.

anna_dev: Good catch. How do we enforce reuse in the synthetic runner?

mike_infra: For HTTP1 we need keepalive + connection pooling. For gRPC use a single long-lived channel with many HTTP/2 streams. Example for our go client:
```go
conn, _ := grpc.Dial(addr, grpc.WithTransportCredentials(creds), grpc.WithKeepaliveParams(keepalive.ClientParameters{/*...*/}))
// reuse conn across goroutines
```

sarah_sre: Also ensure TCP_NODELAY is set. We had micro-batches suffer from Nagle aggregation adding ~2-4ms.

jiwon_ml: Another KV cache gotcha: the replay harness normalizes prompt prefixes but the synthetic client sometimes injects metadata header which changes the cache key -> increases KV misses and causes decoder steps to be longer.

perf-ci: FYI I pushed a small script that compares connection reuse metrics: `tcp_conn_reuse.py` (counts established vs new TLS). Running it against both harnesses made the problem obvious (replay reused, synthetic didn't).

anna_dev: Can someone paste the flame graph from the slower run? I want to see if time is in kernel selection, memcpy, or TLS.

mike_infra: Paste from perf agent:
```
# slow run flame slice
30% TLS handshake (user)
20% kernel_select (runtime)
15% memcpy (cpu -> gpu)
10% batch_queue_wait
25% gpu_infer
```

anna_dev: So TLS + kernel_select are big. That matches the hypothesis: client config causing different request grouping and extra TLS cost.

sarah_sre: For short requests we should recommend: keep a pool of 8-16 persistent connections, use HTTP/2 grpc channels, TCP_NODELAY on, and disable per-request TLS renegotiation. Also set `SO_REUSEPORT` on the client side when creating many processes.

jiwon_ml: On the runtime side we can reduce the cliff by making kernel selection less brittle: add hysteresis so single stray request doesn't flip kernels mid-batch. Also improved batching heuristic to prefer stable latency SLOs over raw throughput.

anna_dev: Plan: 1) fix synthetic client to reuse connections and toggle TCP_NODELAY; 2) re-run both harnesses; 3) add a replay config that intentionally varies inter-arrival jitter to stress kernel selection. Any volunteers to run step1?

mike_infra: I'll update the runner in the next hour. Will post results.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for build r-2026.03.18-harness-fixes :rocket:

perf-ci: After connection reuse fix, p50 aligns (replay 19ms vs synthetic 21ms). Remaining delta ~2ms from Nagle and minor kernel selection jitter.

anna_dev: Nice. Let's capture this as a checklist for docs: client benchmarking pitfalls (keepalive, pool size, grpc vs rest, tcp_nodelay, so_reuseport), replay normalization (exact prompt, headers), and runtime mitigations (kernel hysteresis, batching thresholds). I'll open a short RFC. :memo:
